chapter: Moten band, arranging and the guitar
title: Homemade amplified guitar and the clothes-hanger bridge
summary: Durham explains rigging an amplifier and mike to his guitar and a clothes-hanger swinging bridge, a few years before factory electric guitars.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Well, now, what I want to get to here is, when do you start playing the amplified guitar?
That was with -- let me see, I had my own homemade guitar.
When you say homemade, what was it made of?
Well, I rigged it up so it could be like a -- I had a -- I used accoustic.
Yeah.
Honey, Keep Your Mind On Me, in '38.
Yeah.
But even on the record, I did the same thing. But in the dance hall, we would have to get the mike.
Yeah.
(the guitars)

And lean it over. So finally, I figured out a way to get old amplifier, and got a mike and sometimes used to get the little thing, make them up and put them together and that amplifies that on the stage, run it and get it into the guitar, right in the , hook it in the guitar someplace, and that's the way I could play. And that's how I got that.

Now, with the resonator guitar, always wanted to get wooden (inaudible). So I took a clothes hanger and I attached that to the bridge. Nobody ever saw that, and I used to hook it in this finger. When I'd play, I'd shake it.
How is it fixed? This is just two bits of wire?
I'd take a stiff clothes hanger --
Yeah.
-- and hook it on my finger, and hook it to the bridge or to the top.
Yeah.
And when I hit a chord, this finger here would --
Oh, I see, (inaudible) jangle.
Yeah, but I kept -- not the stationary

bridge, I'd always have the swinging bridge, just hook on back there and over, move it like that. So, about two or three years later, they came out with something already made like that, in the electric guitar. But I didn't pay any attention, I just say, well, (inaudible). But lately, I thought about it, I say I did do that two or three years before they even got into it, before they found that they wanted to do that.
Yeah.
Now they build it in the foot pedal, anywhere. Just touch it and you got it.
Yeah.

But a lot of those things -- I have to hear them, they were made with all type of guitars, different deals. My resonator at the time -- I wore it out, so by the time I got ready to get another one, they was all out of business and the neck was too thick for later stuff, so you had to --
